title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents (BMC ch. 13.63, Ord. 7,992-N.S.)
requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or provide, coordinated pricing algorithms that use nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Each month and each unit is a separate violation.
requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden usar, y los proveedores no pueden vender ni ofrecer, algoritmos de precios coordinados que usan datos no públicos de competidores para fijar o recomendar alquileres u ocupación en viviendas residenciales de Berkeley. Cada mes y cada unidad cuenta como una infracción separada.
key_value: ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for setting rents or occupancy levels
penalty: City Attorney may seek damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees; aggrieved tenants may seek injunctive relief, money damages, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees
coverage_conditions: Applies to residential dwelling units in Berkeley and to sale or provision of such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
exemptions: Excludes products that publish aggregated anonymous rental data without recommending rents, products used to set affordable housing rent or income limits, and products used for market research for project financing, appraisal, or software research, testing or training.
quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
interaction: Document shows the ordinance only passed to print on November 18, 2025; final adoption and effective date are not shown, so effective_date is null. It amends an existing chapter 13.63. It does not regulate the amount of rent.

title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions, and must give written notice and a chance to respond before acting on criminal history.
requirement_es: Los propietarios de Berkeley no pueden preguntar sobre los antecedentes penales ni usarlos en la publicidad, las solicitudes, la selección de inquilinos o sus decisiones, y deben dar aviso por escrito y la oportunidad de responder antes de actuar con base en ellos.
key_value: ban on inquiring about or using criminal history in rental housing decisions
penalty: administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief
coverage_conditions: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley with respect to current or prospective tenants.
exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record resides in one unit as primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

title: Berkeley tenant screening and application fee rules (BMC ch. 13.78)
requirement: Landlords who charge a screening fee must give a screening fee rights statement and the state fee cap before taking the fee. They cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to add, replace or remove a roommate.

coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley, regardless of contrary lease language.

title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance – Measure BB 5% cap on Annual General Adjustment
requirement: Landlords of fully covered Berkeley units may raise rent each year only by the Annual General Adjustment set by the Rent Board, which can never exceed 5%. Government-owned or subsidized units must now be registered and, if fully covered, are subject to the rent ceiling.
requirement_es: Los propietarios de unidades totalmente cubiertas en Berkeley solo pueden aumentar la renta cada año según el Ajuste General Anual fijado por la Junta de Alquileres, que nunca puede superar el 5 %. Las unidades de propiedad gubernamental o subsidiadas ahora deben registrarse y, si están totalmente cubiertas, están sujetas al límite de renta.
key_value: Annual General Adjustment (CPI-based formula), maximum 5%
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies that began prior to 1996, and single-family homes with five or more rooms rented individually. Government-subsidized units are fully or partially covered depending on unit type and whether law prohibits rent control.
exemptions: New construction units (certificate of occupancy issued after 1980), most single-family homes and most condominiums are only partially covered (no rent ceiling). Units with Section 202, Section 811, and HUD-insured/held Section 8-type subsidies are partially covered. Banked AGAs may exceed 5% to reach the rent ceiling.
citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance (Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.76), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

title: California AB 12 security deposit cap
requirement: Starting July 1, 2024, most landlords may charge a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, furnished or unfurnished. Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four units total, held by a natural person, family trust, or all-natural-person LLC, may charge up to two months' rent.
requirement_es: A partir del 1 de julio de 2024, la mayoría de los propietarios solo pueden cobrar un depósito de seguridad de un mes de renta, con o sin muebles. Los propietarios que poseen solo dos propiedades de alquiler con no más de cuatro unidades en total, a nombre de una persona física, un fideicomiso familiar o una LLC cuyos miembros sean todos personas físicas, pueden cobrar hasta dos meses de renta.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND)
requirement: Housing providers with DND funding or land, or with income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, may not use a blanket ban on applicants with arrests or convictions and must review applicants case by case. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, convictions with judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old, and may not use credit scores to approve or deny applications.
requirement_es: Los proveedores de vivienda que reciben fondos o terrenos del DND, o que tienen unidades con ingresos restringidos bajo la Política de Desarrollo Inclusivo de la BPDA, no pueden aplicar una prohibición general a solicitantes con arrestos o condenas y deben evaluar cada caso individualmente. No pueden considerar arrestos sin condena, condenas con alivio judicial, registros juveniles ni condenas de más de 5 años, y no pueden usar puntajes de crédito para aprobar o rechazar solicitudes.
key_value: No blanket ban; no consideration of non-conviction arrests, expunged/sealed convictions, juvenile records, convictions over 5 years old; no credit score use
coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.
exemptions: Criminal-history limits do not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others, or to current criminal behavior. Federal or state law with conflicting criminal history requirements preempts the policy.
citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)

title: California Fair Employment and Housing Act – source-of-income and criminal-history screening limits
requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent or apply different terms because of how you pay rent, including Section 8 vouchers, and must complete paperwork for rental assistance programs. They also cannot consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot impose blanket bans on people with a criminal history.

title: California residential security deposit cap
requirement: A landlord cannot demand or receive security (deposit, fee or charge) above one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. Los arrendadores pequeños (personas físicas o LLC compuestas solo por personas físicas que posean no más de dos propiedades con cuatro unidades en total) pueden cobrar hasta dos meses de renta, pero no a militares en servicio.
key_value: 1 month's rent maximum (2 months for small landlords)
penalty: Bad faith claim or retention may subject the landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages; landlord loses right to claim security if it fails in bad faith to comply with return/itemization rules.
